newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VALENCIA STILL HOPEFUL OF PLACE IN SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VALENCIA STILL HOPEFUL OF PLACE IN SEMIS.

text.p: Valencia will feel they still have a chance of reaching the UEFA Cup semifinals when they face an injury-hit Schalke in Tuesday's quarter-final second leg.
Schalke, bidding to make a European semifinal for first time in 27 years, won the home leg 2-0.
But Valencia have hit form with consecutive league wins, while Schalke fell 3-0 to Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Saturday.
Schalke coach Huub Stevens warned: "If we sleep through the first 25 minutes as we did against Munich, we'll be in trouble."
But midfielder Olaf Thon pledged his side would shake off their injuries and their sluggish performance against Bayern. "We'll be a different side against Valencia," he said.

Stevens had only 14 fit and eligible players at his disposal in Germany and has had to resort to emergency call-ups, ordering his two U.S. internationals, midfielder Tom Dooley and striker David Wagner, to fly straight to Valencia from Sunday's World Cup qualifier against Canada.
He has also called into his squad two amateurs who have never played in the Bundesliga, Thomas Klaesener und Arnold Dybek.
They are missing both scorers from the first leg, striker Marc Wilmots and defender Thomas Linke, who are suspended.
Czech midfielder Radoslav Latal is highly doubtful with ankle ligament trouble. He hopes to play at least one half but coach Stevens holds out little hope.
Manager Rudi Assauer remains philosophical. "There's no point moaning and griping. We have a huge lead from the first leg, now others will have to pick up the baton and do their bit," he said.

The Spaniards also have their problems and will be without the star of their recent victories, Ariel Ortega. The Argentine midfielder has only recently arrived in Spain and is ineligible for European competition.
Also missing will be defender Vicente Engonga, who picked up his second yellow card of the competition in the first leg.

Valencia will be boosted by the return from suspension of goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta, who redeemed himself with a series of fine saves in Saturday's 4-1 away win over Spanish champions Atletico Madrid after a terrible game the previous week.
Defensive general Patxi Ferreira is also set to return from suspension.
Valencia's run of form has done something to take the pressure off former Real Madrid coach Jorge Valdano and much-criticised club president Paco Roig.
Valencia - Andoni Zubizarreta, Javi Navarro, Jorge Otero, Ivan Campo, Enrique Romero, Xabier Eskurza, Fernando Gomez, Valery Karpin, Claudio Lopez, Goran Vlaovic, Gabriel Moya.
Schalke - Jens Lehmann, Olaf Thon, Johan De Kock, Yves Eigenrauch, Radoslav Latal (or Oliver Held), Jiri Nemec, Andreas Mueller, Ingo Anderbruegge, Michael Bueskens, Martin Max, Yuri Mulder.
